specs: Not specified in this pilot profile; size is not used by the current model.
Not characterized in this pilot profile; diet is not used by the current model.

Lower Florida Keys acoustic telemetry documents Permit using both shallow nearshore flats (less than 3 m) and deeper Florida Reef Tract habitat (approximately 15–40 m). The study reported that many tagged fish used both habitat types, supporting a connected flats-and-reef framing rather than a flats-only profile.

The lower Florida Keys telemetry study reported reef occupancy peaking from March through September, especially April–May, and interpreted reef use as associated with spawning. Treat this as study-region evidence, not a fully validated South Florida-wide seasonal rule.

species.name: Yellowtail snapper
specs: Typically 2 to 5 lb and 8 to 14 in; up to about 34 in and 11 lb (NOAA Fisheries). Florida state record 8 lb 9 oz.

Adults mostly 10-70 m over sandy areas near offshore reefs (NOAA Fisheries); commercial handline catch mainly 20-60 m; overall depth range 0-180 m (FishBase). Juveniles use seagrass, mangroves and back reefs.
Reef fish found around coral heads, patch reefs and high-profile artificial structure. Often swarms up a steady chum slick. Juveniles use seagrass and mangrove nursery habitat.
April through August in the southeast U.S. (SAFMC); FishBase notes spawning occurs year-round in parts of the range with different peaks by area
6 to 14 years typical; up to 28 years (NOAA Fisheries)
